idh.reasoning: The metadata favor IDH-wildtype because age_years is 71, and an older adult presentation is more typical of IDH-wildtype diffuse astrocytic glioma than IDH-mutant glioma. The presence of contrast-enhancing tumor and necrotic/non-enhancing tumor components, reflected by ET Volume (mL), Proportion Enhancing, NCR Volume (mL), Proportion Necrosis, Thickness of enhancing margin, and Enhancement Quality, also supports a more aggressive IDH-wildtype phenotype. The large edema component, shown by ED Volume (mL), Proportion of Oedema, and Edema crosses midline, further supports this direction. Features arguing against IDH-wildtype include Cortical involvement, absence of Deep WM invasion, mild Enhancement Quality rather than florid enhancement, Solitary disease without Multiple satellites present, absent Ependymal (ventricular) Invasion, and only Minimal midline_shift_present, which can be seen in lower-grade or IDH-mutant tumors. On balance, the age and enhancing/necrotic/edematous phenotype outweigh the milder, more circumscribed features, so the best estimate is IDH-wildtype.

one_p_nineteen_q.reasoning: The metadata favor 1p/19q non-codeletion because age_years is 71 and Tumor Location/Region Proportions indicate a predominantly parietal-cortical-occipital lesion rather than a classic frontal-predominant oligodendroglioma pattern. The presence of measurable enhancement and necrotic/non-enhancing tumor components, reflected by ET Volume (mL), Proportion Enhancing, NCR Volume (mL), Proportion Necrosis, Thickness of enhancing margin, and Enhancement Quality, is less typical for a classic lower-grade 1p/19q-codeleted oligodendroglioma phenotype, although enhancement can occur in oligodendroglioma. The large edema component shown by ED Volume (mL), Proportion of Oedema, and Edema crosses midline also supports a non-codeleted high-grade astrocytic-type process. Features arguing against non-codeletion include Cortical involvement, mild Enhancement Quality, absence of Deep WM invasion and Ependymal (ventricular) Invasion, and Solitary disease without Multiple satellites present, which do not exclude oligodendroglioma. Overall, because the lesion is elderly-onset, non-frontal, enhancing/necrotic, and markedly edematous, the best estimate is non-codeleted.

overall_comment: Predictions are based only on structured conventional MRI metadata without diffusion, perfusion, spectroscopy, susceptibility/calcification assessment, or histology. Molecular testing remains required, especially because mild enhancement and cortical involvement are not specific.

who_grade.reasoning: The metadata favor CNS WHO grade 4 because there is a contrast-enhancing component and a necrotic/non-enhancing component, reflected by ET Volume (mL), Proportion Enhancing, NCR Volume (mL), Proportion Necrosis, Thickness of enhancing margin, and Enhancement Quality; necrosis and enhancement on conventional MRI are strong markers of high-grade diffuse glioma. The large edema burden, shown by ED Volume (mL), Proportion of Oedema, and Edema crosses midline, also supports high-grade behavior. Features arguing against grade 4 include mild Enhancement Quality, relatively limited Proportion Enhancing and Proportion Necrosis, Minimal midline_shift_present, absent Asymmetrical Ventricles, absent Ependymal (ventricular) Invasion, absent Deep WM invasion, Solitary disease without Multiple satellites present, and modest Lesion Sizes APxTVxCC (cm), which could fit grade 2 or 3 glioma. Nevertheless, the presence of measurable enhancement plus necrotic/non-enhancing tumor and extensive edema makes grade 4 the best estimate from the available MRI metadata.
